data.narrative: The student built a complete environment configuration system using zod schema validation that crashes immediately at startup when any required variable is absent. They demonstrated strong failure-thinking by identifying and fixing three configuration anti-patterns — unsafe localhost defaults, an unguarded dotenv call, and a missing CORS_ORIGIN requirement — proving each fix with concrete command output. The student correctly articulated that configuration errors carry the same user impact as security breaches, showing production-oriented reasoning beyond the immediate coding task.

dimension_scores.observation: Verified Docker image is free of .env files using docker run --rm ls -la, confirmed .dockerignore excludes .env* glob, and ensured no environment-specific values are baked into the image.
dimension_scores.evidence: docker run --rm api-envtest ls -la — grep exits 1 (no .env found). Image sha rebuilt to 47ff59c4.

dimension_scores.observation: Correctly scoped dotenv.config() so it loads .env without overriding platform-injected env vars, confirmed with Docker -e flag test showing 'injected env (0) from .env' inside container.
dimension_scores.evidence: Docker run with -e NODE_ENV=staging produced startup log environment=staging, cors_origin=https://staging.example.com with zero .env values loaded inside container.

dimension_scores.observation: Added startup log that announces environment, port, log_level, and cors_origin — non-secret values only. Explicitly commented why MONGODB_URI and JWT_SECRET are excluded from logs.
dimension_scores.evidence: Startup log output: {message: Service starting, environment: production, port: 3002, log_level: info, cors_origin: https://app.example.com} — no secrets present.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified 3 bugs unprompted: (1) localhost default for CORS_ORIGIN silently breaks production browser traffic, (2) PORT default masks misconfiguration, (3) dotenv running unconditionally in production. Articulated that configuration mistakes equal security vulnerabilities from the user's perspective.
dimension_scores.evidence: Removed CORS_ORIGIN default and made it REQUIRED. Missing CORS_ORIGIN now crashes: CORS_ORIGIN: { _errors: [ 'Invalid input: expected string, received undefined' ] }

dimension_scores.observation: Implemented fail-fast pattern correctly — service calls process.exit(1) before NestJS boots when any required config is absent, preventing partial initialization with broken state.
dimension_scores.evidence: config import is first line in main.ts before NestFactory.create() — if config fails, NestJS never initializes. Confirmed by /tmp test: service exits with named error, never reaches route registration.

dimension_scores.observation: Created .env.example with REQUIRED/OPTIONAL annotations, example values, security warning about committing .env, and openssl command for JWT_SECRET generation. Comments explain the purpose of each variable group.
dimension_scores.evidence: .env.example includes: 'NEVER commit .env to git. Only .env.example belongs in version control. If .env was ever committed, the secrets in it are compromised — rotate them.'

strengths: Fail-fast implementation: config validation runs before NestJS boots, confirmed with /tmp test showing immediate crash naming the missing variable
Security reasoning: correctly identified that configuration errors (APP_ENV=development in prod) have identical user impact to attacks — not prompted, volunteered this insight
Docker verification: proactively confirmed image cleanliness with docker run --rm ls -la rather than relying on .dockerignore inspection alone
data.recommendation: In Module 04, apply the same fail-fast mindset to observability — define what must be logged (request_id, latency, error codes) and what must never be logged (secrets, PII) before writing any logging code.

public_evidence.student_action: Built env validation module using zod schema with required fields (NODE_ENV enum, MONGODB_URI, JWT_SECRET min-32, CORS_ORIGIN) and safe defaults for PORT and LOG_LEVEL. Import is first line of main.ts so service crashes before NestJS boots on any misconfiguration.
public_evidence.technical_detail: envSchema.safeParse(process.env) + process.exit(1) on failure, imported before NestFactory.create()
public_evidence.proof: cd /tmp && NODE_ENV=development PORT=3000 JWT_SECRET=local-dev-jwt-secret-key-min-32-chars-ok node /api/dist/main.js => ❌ Invalid environment configuration: MONGODB_URI: { _errors: [ 'Invalid input: expected string, received undefined' ] }
public_evidence.ability: Implements fail-fast startup validation for environment configuration
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates production awareness: a service that refuses to boot on misconfiguration is safer than one that starts silently with wrong values

public_evidence.student_action: Created complete .env.example with REQUIRED/OPTIONAL annotations, example values, security warning, and secret generation instructions. Updated .gitignore and .dockerignore to exclude .env*.
public_evidence.technical_detail: .env* in .dockerignore glob, .env in .gitignore, .env.example committed to git
public_evidence.proof: docker run --rm api-envtest ls -la /app — grep exits 1 (no .env file found in image)
public_evidence.ability: Documents environment contracts and enforces secrets-out-of-image principle
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows understanding that the Docker image must be environment-agnostic and that .env.example is the onboarding contract for new team members

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: config.ts imported first in main.ts, zod safeParse + process.exit(1), confirmed crash before NestJS initializes
Verified with docker run --rm ls -la — no .env in container. .dockerignore uses .env* glob.
Docker -e flags produced environment=staging in startup log with injected env (0) from .env

teaching_approaches.detail: Real incident: e-commerce batch delete wiped 12,000 records because staging pointed at prod DB via wrong connection string

learning_style_signals: responds well to concrete failure scenarios
